messages:
felix: Quick sync: I prototyped a "prov token" emitted by the edge proxy to help later-cost attribution when sampling/batching removes tenant-level metadata. Want feedback on format and rollout constraints.

felix: Motivation: we often can't link compacted traces back to billing keys. Late-enrich lookups spike and queries return low-confidence attribution. A tiny stable token would let us deterministically stitch most events without full-key lookups.

felix: Prototype format: `rdwd-prov=v2:<region-code>:<cohort24>:<sig6>` e.g. `rdwd-prov=v2:eu:c5g9k:3f2a1b` where cohort24 is base32(24bit) and sig6 is truncated HMAC for tamper-resistance. Total header ~28 bytes.

amy: Why v2? what's changed from v1 sketches?

felix: v1 was raw hash+cohort. v2 adds a short region tag and a 6-char signature so we can detect forged tokens and avoid accepting tokens from other clusters during cross-region replays.

sam: Are we okay relying on truncated HMAC? Collisions? Attack surface? If someone can observe tokens, could they infer tenant density or do targeted traffic?

felix: We considered that. We never include tenant ids or raw keys. Cohorts are intentionally coarse (24-bit space -> ~16M). Signature uses region-scoped key rotated weekly. Risk model: token leakage reveals only cohort membership and region; not sufficient to enumerate tenants. Legal review suggested documenting this tradeoff.

olga: Operational question: where do we compute cohort? On the proxy (lua) or upstream service? Doing it at proxy saves roundtrips, but increases CPU on edge fleet.

felix: Prototype used lua in nginx. CPU overhead measured ~0.1% p95 on our small test bed. We can optimize by computing only for requests that hit sampling/batching thresholds or when a header isn't already present.

sam: Cache/keying implications for runtime: does the runtime need to include the token in cache keys so that cached responses maintain attribution?

felix: Short answer: yes for any per-tenant metrics we emit. Implementation: runtime adds token to telemetry context and, if response emits metrics, attach token. For caches we can include a 6-bit cohort suffix to avoid exploding cardinality.

amy: Metrics to watch during canary: token-presence-rate, cohort-cardinality-by-region, enrich-late-qps, attribution-stability (changes/week), and probe-sampled-precision. Also monitor request size regressions for mobile carriers.

olga: Rollout idea: 1) emit header only (no indexing) to EU canaries 2) sample raw billing keys 0.01% and correlate with prov tokens to estimate precision/FP 3) if ok, enable platform-side join for a subset of services 4) expand. We should have an immediate kill-switch in edge config to stop emitting header.

sam: How does this interact with private installs? Some customers won't allow any provenance tokens leaving their VPC. We need a config flag and clear docs. For hosted default on, private default off.

felix: Agreed. We'll add a config knob per-tenant and document privacy tradeoffs. Also add an option to hash with customer-provided salt on private installs so platform can't resolve tokens.

amy: Ownership: eng-platform builds the resolution service and telemetry-side ingestion logic. eng-runtime will accept header and include it in emitted telemetry and caches. eng-infra to provide key rotation endpoint for signatures.

infra-bot: rollout-ticket created: https://go/redwood/tickets/PRV-2043 :ticket:

felix: Final open questions before RFC: 1) exact token encoding (base32 vs base64 urlsafe) 2) cohort bit-width (24 vs 20) 3) sig length (6 vs 8 chars) 4) default for private installs. Would love quick thumbs.

olga: My picks: base32 (human-friendly), 20 bits (less cardinality blowup), sig8 (safer), private-default-off.

sam: +1 to olga but prefer sig6 if we care about header size on constrained links.

amy: I'm OK with sig8; we can compress region and cohort to keep size similar.

felix: Thanks all — I'll bake this into the RFC draft with the choices noted and include a lightweight privacy appendix. Planning to open RFC Tue morning and tag reviewers. Closing thread for now.
